title: What Actually Counts as a True AI Agent?
summary:
Not every chatbot, workflow, or LLM wrapper is an AI agent.

In this Short, Micheal Lanham, author of AI Agents in Action, Second Edition, explains what makes an AI system truly agentic: autonomy, goals, reasoning, tool use, feedback, and the ability to act in an environment. He also calls out what we should probably stop calling “agents.”

Learn more about the book: https://hubs.la/Q04p-7WX0

title: EXPOSED: Meta's Story Kit Turns Your Child's Toy Into an AI Story

title: Stop LLM LOOPS From Burning Millions of Tokens - w/ PUMA?
summary:
When allowing LLMs to "think" longer via test-time scaling (Chain-of-Thought), models often enter "cognitive stagnation": endlessly generating repetitive or vacuous tokens without making progress. 

Existing efficiency filters fail: entropy-based methods are tricked by "confident hallucinations" (low entropy, high confidence, wrong answer), and latent-based methods are computationally prohibitive because they evaluate completed trajectories post-hoc.

The authors (see below) present a new solution. 
The End of AI Overthinking and burning millions of tokens in a low entropy loop for no real result?

Existing efficiency filters fail: entropy-based methods are tricked by "confident hallucinations" (low entropy, high confidence, wrong answer), and latent-based methods are computationally prohibitive because they evaluate completed trajectories post-hoc.

The authors (see below) present a new solution. 
The End of AI Overthinking and burning millions of tokens in a low entropy loop for no real result?

title: Graph Engineering Explained, Without the Hype
summary:

► My Newsletter (My AI updates and news clearly explained): https://louisbouchard.substack.com/

Graph engineering is the latest term spreading through AI Twitter, but the useful idea is how we structure work once one agent loop is not enough. In this video, I unpack Peter Steinberger's viral post and Hamel Husain's X Article, explain how retry cycles fit inside general directed workflows, and show what multi-agent orchestration looks like with Claude Code and Codex. We also cover the failure mode most diagrams ignore: reviewers built from the same model and context can share correlated blind spots. The practical takeaway is how to design state, parallel branches, outside verification, vetoes, budgets, and hard stops without building a forty-agent token furnace.

title: How Does Local Hardware Help Avoid Recurring Subscription Costs?
summary:
Cloud AI bills can add up fast.

In this short, Keiji Kamigusa explains how local hardware can help developers avoid recurring subscription costs by running AI models directly on a Mac they already own.

Instead of paying every month for every experiment, prompt, document workflow, or API call, local AI lets you build and test private chatbots, RAG apps, voice tools, and other AI-powered projects on your own machine.

That doesn’t mean cloud AI goes away. It means you get options: use the cloud when it makes sense, and use local models when privacy, control, or long-term cost matters more.

Build Applications with Local AI Models on a Mac shows you how to turn your Mac into a practical local AI development environment.

Learn more: https://hubs.la/Q04mY6wQ0

title: EXPOSED: Can India Build Its Own SpaceX? The Private Space Race Begins | Point Break
summary:
India's private space sector has reached orbit, but the harder challenge is still ahead: turning one historic launch into a repeatable, commercially sustainable ecosystem of rockets, satellites, space infrastructure and deep-tech companies.

In this episode of Point Break, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Professor Shrea Santra, Head of Research at Sarabhai Spaceport, and Anurag Beluri, Head of Partnerships at Take Me To Space, to break down Skyroot Aerospace's first-attempt orbital success, the policy shift that opened India's space sector to private companies, the rise of more than 400 space-tech startups, the role of young engineers and former ISRO scientists, the case for reusable rockets, the importance of patient capital, and the path from technical demonstrations to commercial scale. The discussion also examines whether India can build an ecosystem capable of producing multiple multi-billion-dollar space companies.

title: HUGE: India's Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Won't Wait for Japan Anymore

title: BREAKING: India's Stock Exchanges Just Stopped Relying on Foreign GPS Time
summary:
India just commissioned a demonstration network using precision timing technology built for the Large Hadron Collider at CERN, aiming to end its financial markets' dependence on foreign GPS time signals. The network distributes Indian Standard Time using White Rabbit technology, the same protocol that synchronises CERN's particle collisions, offering sub-nanosecond, picosecond-level accuracy across banking, telecom, and stock exchanges.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down how NSE and BSNL tested the system, why compromised timing signals threaten trade sequencing and transaction records, and what India's broader One Nation One Time initiative means for financial sovereignty.

title: Anthropic's New J-Space: Debunked?
summary:
Anthropic is mapping a neuroscience theory to their LLMs. Why? And why build a Jacobian Lens for Claude? What is this J-Space? A new discovery by Anthropic? 

My working definition of J-space:
A union of many sparse nonnegative cones constructed from an overcomplete dictionary of non-orthogonal token directions. There is no evidence for a demonstrated consciousness or "central thought space" for AI systems.

Note: The Jacobian also provides only first-order information. Higher order terms might contribute but are neglected.

title: HUGE: Anthropic Gives Researchers $50K to Use Claude for Rare Diseases
summary:
Anthropic is opening a new round of its AI for Science program, offering researchers and biotechs up to 50,000 dollars in Claude credits over the next 6 months to work on rare diseases. The core problem is clear: 7000 known rare diseases affect an estimated 400 million people worldwide. Individually rare. Collectively, one of medicine's biggest unsolved problems.

✅ Chess League: Test your skills → https://chess.analyticsindiamag.com/

Rare diseases are scattered across small isolated patient populations, making it nearly impossible to build patient registries for clinical trials. Each condition is defined by unique symptoms studied in isolation, making it hard to spot disease mechanisms shared across different rare conditions that could point toward shared treatment. Anthropic's program splits into two tracks. Basic scientists work to understand mechanisms using Monarch Initiative's Disease Ontology, which links genotype and phenotype data across species.

title: BREAKING: Google Hardwires Gemini Into Silicon to Tackle Compute Shortage
summary:
Google is developing Frozen V2, a custom AI chip that hardwires parts of Gemini's architecture directly into hardware. Unlike today's general-purpose TPUs that load models into memory and shuttle data back and forth, Frozen V2 bakes the neural network blueprint into the silicon itself. This reduces calculations and data travel, potentially serving 6 to 10 times more AI tokens per unit of power compared to Google's newest TPUs.

✅ Cypher 2026: Join 5,000+ AI leaders. Book now → https://cypher.analyticsindiamag.com/tickets
✅ Chess League: Test your skills → https://chess.analyticsindiamag.com/

The original concept from Google DeepMind's Jeff Dean locked in actual model weights, but that approach would have tied the chip to a single Gemini release. Frozen V2 is more flexible. It hardwires the underlying blueprint but lets engineers load new weights as needed. Google is dealing with a serious internal AI compute shortage, reportedly even paying SpaceX close to a billion dollars monthly to help bridge that gap. Frozen V2 is meant to ease that pressure by squeezing more useful AI output from hardware Google already has. Deployment is targeted for 2028. Investors liked what they heard, with Alphabet shares jumping 3.77% intraday on the news.

title: Building time crystals with quantum computers
summary:
Crystals are defined by repeating patterns—but what if those patterns unfold in time rather than space? In this episode of The Coherence Times, we take a closer look at “time crystals”—systems of interacting particles that exhibit unique behaviors when driven by regular pulses of energy.

Join host Ryan Mandelbaum as they speak with Dr. Eric Switzer and Dr. Nicolás Lorente, two researchers who recently used IBM’s quantum computers to create and study a two-dimensional time crystal. Together, they break down what it means for a system to behave like a crystal in time, why studying systems out of equilibrium matters, and how quantum computers enable experiments that go beyond the limitations of purely classical methods.

title: ALERT: Seoul Semiconductor's India Plant Could Be Built in Months, Not Years
summary:
Five days after Semicon 2.0 was approved with ₹1,27,500 crore backing, Seoul Semiconductor confirmed it's assessing a manufacturing plant in India. The Korean LED and opto-electronics giant just triggered a three-state bidding war between Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Gujarat. This is Seoul's first India production base ever. It currently manufactures only in South Korea, the US, China, and Vietnam.

Here's what matters: this isn't a chip fab. It's an assembly and packaging unit, which needs far less capital, water, and construction time. If greenlit, it could go from board approval to production in months, not years. Seoul ranks 3rd globally in LED semiconductors, holds 18,000+ patents, and was the only top-three player to hold both revenue and market share through the 2024 LED downturn. Korean chip suppliers are officially diversifying away from China concentration toward India's growing electronics market, and this deal signals they mean business.

title: ALERT: Paytm's Board Rejected Bonus Shares Even With ₹222 Crore Quarterly Profit
summary:
Paytm's board made a counterintuitive call after delivering blockbuster Q1 results. With consolidated net profit up 78.8% year-on-year to ₹222 crore and operating revenue growing 27.6% to ₹2,448 crore, investors expected a bonus share announcement. Instead, the board rejected it. The board's reasoning was direct: in a company that only recently turned consistently profitable, capital discipline matters more than a stock price sugar rush.

The company approved an additional ₹100 crore investment in wholly-owned subsidiary Paytm Money to fuel technology and regulatory capital needs. It also asked shareholders to extend the deadline for deploying leftover IPO funds to March 2029, reallocating capital toward core payments and strengthening the finserve ecosystem. In a leadership update, Google Search's former SVP Amitabh Kumar Singh joined as a non-executive director.

title: HUGE: Wipro Flat, HCL Soars - Indian IT's AI Earnings Revealed a Winner and a Loser
summary:
India's largest IT services companies held earnings calls this quarter with an unprecedented tone shift. For three decades, the model was predictable: land a multi-year contract, build an offshore team, and renew repeatedly. Now TCS CEO Kitiasan put it bluntly: most AI projects last one to two quarters maximum, forcing firms back to the market every cycle to hunt new deals. Meanwhile, HCL Tech reported 13.9% revenue growth, Wipro posted 0.9% flat growth, and Tech Mahindra led with 17.7% growth, signals that not all Indian IT giants are equal in the AI transition.

In this editorial interview, host Sudhi Sachdev from AIM speaks with tech journalist Ajay Rag to explore what broke the 30-year model: outcome-based pricing vs. labor arbitrage, the rise of forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) as a new job title, token costs becoming a core business metric, and whether HCL Tech's $150 million bet on Serum and data center ownership represents the future or a distraction. The gap between supply and demand for FD talent is severe, and candidates need far more than coding skills, client relations, problem-solving, and sector expertise are now table stakes.

title: Sandboxing, Agent Harnesses, and Agent Teamwork
summary:
Shahram Anver is the Co-Founder and CEO of Cleric, the autonomous AI SRE that investigates and root-causes production issues like an experienced teammate — often in under two minutes. Before Cleric, Shahram led MLOps, DevOps, and FinOps platform engineering at Gojek, Southeast Asia's super-app. In this conversation, he breaks down why production operations never kept pace with AI-accelerated development, and why the real unlock for an AI SRE isn't faster triage — it's an agent that *learns* and compounds operational memory across your whole org.

title: From LOOPS to GRAPHS: AI Agents Learn Graph-Based Error Corrections
summary:
From LOOPS to GRAPHS.

Test-time RAG, prompt injection, skill.md files, Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) algorithm, training-time graph-theoretical mathematics. Negative knowledge patterns,  highly specific IF-THEN conditional rules.

Language Models as Agents are too brittle if left to figure everything out on the fly.
MemoHarness introduces Dynamic System Configuration.
EMG introduces Algorithmic Error Routing.

Start with MemoHarness RAG-based control layer to dynamically configure the agent's memory and tools, and then you would use EMG's graph-matching inside the agent's procedural memory to ensure it executes the precise sequence of actions without needing costly reflection loops.

title: 6-dim Harness w/ MEMORY via Textual Gradients
summary:
What happens when an AI agent stops using one fixed control system for every problem? 

This new research shows how a frozen LLM can reuse execution experience to reconfigure its own context, tools, memory, orchestration, and output strategy for each new task: without retraining its weights. 

The result is a shift from static agents toward adaptive computational systems that learn not only what to answer, but how to organize themselves (!) before answering.

title: Why TikTok Beats TV, But Not In India - Santosh Nair Explains, After Tracking $3.8B In Ad Spend
summary:
TikTok may appear to deliver stronger short-term ROI than television, but Santosh Nair explains why marketing measurement needs to account for the entire consumer journey.

In this episode of Simulated Reality, Santosh Nair, Senior Vice President & Co-Head of Analytic Edge, explains how companies measure advertising effectiveness across television, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok. title: User Conversations: Dmitry Sizov
summary: From modeling a medieval trebuchet to launching spacecraft, Dmitriy shares how the Wolfram Language reshaped the way he thinks as an engineer and educator. In this conversation, he traces his journey from that first 2013 encounter with symbolic computation to building fully interactive Aerospace Engineering lectures in Mathematica, deriving equations on the fly, simulating orbital maneuvers, and visualizing structural behavior in real time. He also discusses the custom tools he's built, including a beam solver for structural mechanics and research packages for orbital and rotational dynamics. More than a workflow upgrade, Dmitriy explains how the shift from procedural to functional thinking transformed the way he solves problems, teaches students, and approaches engineering itself. A must-watch for engineers, educators, and anyone curious about the power of computational thinking.

title: Fable 5 as Advisor: Anthropic's Two-Model Pattern for Smarter, Cheaper Agents (Ep. 1010)
summary:
In Episode #1010, @JonKrohnLearns digs into “the advisor strategy”, a clever pattern that pairs a fast, cheap executor model with a frontier-class advisor it can consult mid-task, all inside a single API call. Every agent builder faces the same tension: frontier models plan best but cost too much to run on every turn, while small models fumble the decisions that matter. Anthropic’s advisor tool resolves it with roughly a one-line code change, and the benchmarks are startling: Sonnet with an Opus advisor scored higher than Sonnet alone while costing 11.9% less, and Haiku’s BrowseComp score more than doubled at 85% lower cost than Sonnet solo. Jon covers the newest Fable 5 numbers, the practical gotchas, how it differs from OpenAI’s router, and why AI progress is now as much about composing models as training bigger ones.

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1010

title: AI Agents Code Their Own Harness Optimization
summary:
What happens when a frontier LLM (GPT, Claude) is surrounded by an editable harness: and separate solver, debugger, and meta-agent roles are allowed to iteratively rewrite its prompts, memory, middleware, verification gates, tool interfaces, and control logic using execution traces and benchmark feedback? 

My video dissects the full outer-loop optimization system, formalizes how harness search differs from trajectory-level test-time scaling, and examines the experimental protocol required to determine whether recursive agent self-modification constitutes genuine architectural improvement ... or merely a more elaborate form of inference-time adaptation.

title: Ever Inherited a System With Unclear Reasoning Behind Its Design, Making Any Change Feel Risky?

Ever opened a legacy system and thought: “Why is it built like this?”

No documentation. No clear tradeoffs. No one remembers the original reasoning. And suddenly every “small change” feels like defusing a bomb.

In this short, Matt Erman, author of Grokking Software Architecture, explains how to approach inherited systems when the architecture decisions aren’t obvious — and how to make changes with more confidence instead of fear.

Because the scariest code isn’t always the messiest code. It’s the code where nobody knows why it works.

title: Omnigent: Composition, Control, and Collaboration for AI Agents
summary:
Denny Lee is PM Director, Startups & Ecosystem at Databricks, a longtime Apache Spark, MLflow, and Delta Lake contributor — and one of the people behind Omnigent, the open-source meta-harness Databricks just released under Apache 2.0. He joins Demetrios to explain why the industry is moving from models to harnesses to meta-harnesses, why token spend is replaying the CapEx-to-OpEx shift all over again, and why he's using debating AI agents to plan a matcha farm in Taiwan.

In this episode:

🍵 Agents as research partners — Denny uses dueling agents to scout matcha-growing regions in Taiwan, down to soil pH, elevation, and processing infrastructure

🥊 Why agents should debate each other — letting two models argue surfaces the questions you didn't know to ask

🔱 Forking conversations — the missing UX pattern: branch a session, keep the shared context, explore two threads in parallel

🧠 The meta-harness layer — how Omnigent sits above Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and custom agents so models and harnesses become hot-swappable parts

👥 The two-pizza rule for agents — military span-of-control logic says you can manage 5–7 agents before you lose the thread

💸 Tokenomics is the new DevOps — the CapEx→OpEx playbook repeats: give developers spend visibility, keep central governance for the rest

🛡️ Policies, budgets, and guardrails — enforcing cost caps and approval rules at the harness layer instead of inside prompts

🤖 Auto model selection — why classic machine learning (not another LLM) may be the right way to route tasks to cheap vs. frontier models

✍️ "Created by" vs. "assisted by" — the open source accountability debate: whoever submits the code owns the code

🗄️ Databases are back — agents need cheap, stateful memory, which is why Postgres, Lakebase, and serverless databases are having a moment

If you're building with coding agents, managing AI spend, or trying to keep up with the harness arms race, this one's for you.

title: First we shape AI, thereafter AI shapes us
summary:
When we put new technology into the world, we need human-centered methods to understand their impact. This talk will present three focus areas of my research in how people use AI and how that shapes them; 1. The cognitive and metacognitive costs of AI, 2. How people red-team LLMs in the wild, and 3. Hacc-Man - an arcade game for fostering AI literacy.

Bio: Nanna Inie, Assistant Professor, IT-University of Copenhagen

People describe Nanna as "a methodological savant", "a Pandora's Box of unfiltered opinions", and "who?" She uses mixed-methods to study how humans use technology to extend their cognition, evaluate how technology affects human cognition in return, and to transform findings into the design of novel technologies.

She is an assistant professor at the IT-University of Copenhagen and a lecturer at the University of Washington. Her specializations are cognitive augmentation tools, computing education, and AI safety in real-world settings.

In Episode #1009, Steve Mock (investor at Blumberg Capital, five-time entrepreneur, and creator of aisavedme.org), joins @JonKrohnLearns to explore the quiet layer of everyday AI adoption that rarely gets documented. After his 84-year-old father asked a deceptively simple question, “How does one use AI?”, Steve built a place for people to share how AI is actually helping them. In Episode #1009, Steve Mock (investor at Blumberg Capital, five-time entrepreneur, and creator of aisavedme.org), joins @JonKrohnLearns to explore the quiet layer of everyday AI adoption that rarely gets documented. After his 84-year-old father asked a deceptively simple question, “How does one use AI?”, Steve built a place for people to share how AI is actually helping them. The stories that came in surprised him: they’re rarely about the technology and almost always about human outcomes, caregiving, communication, learning, confidence and connection.

title: Can a Standard Mac Really Run Sophisticated Models Without Lag?
summary:
Yes, your Mac can do more than you think.

In this short, Keiji Kamigusa answers one of the biggest questions about local AI: can a standard Mac really run sophisticated models without painful lag?

Thanks to Apple Silicon and modern local AI tools, running useful models on your own machine is becoming surprisingly practical. That means you can build private chatbots, RAG apps, voice tools, and other AI applications locally, without defaulting to expensive cloud APIs or a dedicated GPU rig.

Build Applications with Local AI Models on a Mac shows you how to get started with real projects that run on your Mac and help you understand what local AI can actually do.

If you’ve been assuming “my laptop isn’t enough,” this short may change your mind.

title: Try This Awesome AI Video Transition!
summary:
How to "Time Travel" in your next video with this SUPER easy editing trick!

You don't need complex VFX software to create seamless, mind-bending transitions anymore. Here is a straightforward way to jump between locations using AI tools like Runway, Kling, or Leonardo:

Step 1: Record your intro in Location A, then head to Location B. Try to wear the same outfit and match your pose at the start of the second clip—it makes the final transition much more believable.
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the very last frame of Clip A, and the very first frame of Clip B.
Step 3: Upload these two images as your starting and ending keyframes in an AI tool (I used Runway's Seedance 2.0 for the edit you see in this video).
Step 4: Use a prompt like this: “The camera shoots up like a big jump transition and reveals the second location in one smooth motion. The man does not speak.” (Pro-tip: Adding "does not speak" stops the AI from generating weird facial movements).
Step 5: Download the generated clip, place it between your two original videos, and apply a short crossfade or smooth cut to hide the seams.

This method works for teleporting, outfit changes, mic tosses, and more.

Save this post so you can reference the prompt later, and tag a creator who needs to try this! 🎬

title: The Next Evolution of AI (Qwen, MIT, Tencent)
summary:
Three independent ArXiv pre-prints have converged on the same scientific hypothesis: the limiting factor of frontier AI is no longer inference quality, context length, or even reasoning ability. 

Instead, the next generation of intelligent systems may be defined by their capacity for recursive cognitive organization: the autonomous formation of evidence graphs, the maintenance of coherent long-horizon behavioral trajectories, and ultimately the evolution of their own representational geometry. See also RSI.

My video synthesizes these seemingly unrelated works into a unified theory of AI's next paradigm, arguing that we are witnessing a transition from intelligence as statistical prediction to intelligence as the dynamic self-organization of cognition itself.

The next evolution of AI is not a model that produces better answers inside a fixed problem. It is a system that constructs its evidence, preserves its purpose across time, and reorganizes its own conceptual space when the problem demands it.

title: Reconstructing Pelé’s lost goal
summary:
On August 2, 1959, Pelé scored the most beautiful goal of his career: three consecutive “sombreros” without the ball touching the ground. Yet, the legendary ‘Gol da Rua Javari’ was never caught on film. We worked alongside historians, sports journalists, football legends, and Pelé’s family to reconstruct this lost moment and share it with the world.

This project was created in full partnership with the Pelé Brand, the official managers of the Pelé estate.

Rooted in education and cultural preservation, the project heads to the Pelé Museum this year. To achieve this, teams from Google DeepMind used models like Gemini Omni and Veo to transform historical fragments into moving imagery, filmed on the original pitch with authentic uniforms and a vintage ball.

By making the memory of this goal more accessible, it stands as a tribute to inspire a new generation of fans during the first World Cup without him.

The goal is on display at the Museu Pelé in Santos, Brazil.

Learn more at https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/pele-lost-goal-reconstructed

___

No dia 2 de agosto de 1959, Pelé marcou o gol mais bonito da sua carreira: três chapéus consecutivos, sem deixar a bola tocar no chão. No entanto, o famoso “Gol da Rua Javari” nunca foi filmado. Em um trabalho em conjunto com historiadores, jornalistas esportivos, lendas do futebol e familiares do Pelé, reconstruímos esse momento antológico do futebol para o mundo todo ver.

Esse projeto foi criado em parceria com a marca Pelé, administradores oficiais do espólio do Rei Pelé.

Com foco em educação e preservação cultural, o projeto segue para o Museu Pelé este ano. Para conseguir isso, equipes do Google DeepMind usaram modelos de IA como Gemini Omni e Veo, para transformar fragmentos históricos em filmes, usando filmagens no campo original com uniformes e bola da época.

Tornar a memória desse gol acessível, é uma forma de homenagem, para inspirar as novas gerações de fãs de futebol, na primeira Copa do Mundo sem o Rei Pelé.

O “Gol da Rua Javari” está em exibição no Museu Pelé, em Santos.

title: AI Agents in Action
summary:
Book Launch with Micheal Lanham!! 

With the latest edition of AI Agents in Action you are not just understanding what AI Agents are, but designing, implementing, evaluating, and deploying them.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
1. People build an impressive agent demo, but struggle to make it reliable. What is the biggest gap between a working prototype and a production-ready AI agent?

2. When people say “AI agent,” they often mean very different things. How do you define an agent in the book, and what should developers stop calling an agent?

3. Many developers get stuck after basic prompting. What core components should they understand before trying to build serious agentic systems?

4. Tool use is one of the most exciting parts of agents, but also one of the riskiest. How does Model Context Protocol change the way agents connect to tools, data, and external systems?

5. Multi-agent systems sound powerful, but they can also become chaotic. When should someone use multiple agents instead of one well-designed agent?

6. Planning and reasoning are where agents often look smart until they fail unexpectedly. What are the most common reasoning failures you see, and how can builders design around them?

7. Memory and RAG are often treated as add-ons. In a useful agent, how should memory, knowledge retrieval, and context management actually work together?

8. Evaluation is a major community pain point because agent behavior is hard to test. What should teams measure to know whether an agent is improving or becoming more dangerous?

9. Deployment is where many agent projects stall. What changes when you move from running an agent locally to deploying an agentic system that users or businesses depend on?

10. If someone has read blog posts, watched demos, and tried frameworks but still feels unsure how to build agents properly, how does AI Agents in Action, Second Edition help them move from scattered knowledge to a complete mental model?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Micheal.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #AI to enter the raffle!

5. Multi-agent systems sound powerful, but they can also become chaotic. When should someone use multiple agents instead of one well-designed agent?

6. Planning and reasoning are where agents often look smart until they fail unexpectedly. What are the most common reasoning failures you see, and how can builders design around them?

7. Memory and RAG are often treated as add-ons. In a useful agent, how should memory, knowledge retrieval, and context management actually work together?

8. Evaluation is a major community pain point because agent behavior is hard to test. What should teams measure to know whether an agent is improving or becoming more dangerous?

9. Deployment is where many agent projects stall. What changes when you move from running an agent locally to deploying an agentic system that users or businesses depend on?

10. If someone has read blog posts, watched demos, and tried frameworks but still feels unsure how to build agents properly, how does AI Agents in Action, Second Edition help them move from scattered knowledge to a complete mental model?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Micheal.

title: Watching America Run Away With AI - Alistair Pullen (Cosine AI)
summary:
This episode is sponsored by Notion. Learn more about Notion's Developer Platform today at https://notion.com/mlst

Britain's most capable coding model can't be exported, and that ban is the whole reason Cosine set out to build one from scratch. Alistair Pullen, CEO and co-founder of Cosine, sits down with Tim Scarfe to explain how a frontier system he calls Fable, locked behind US export controls, became the founding case for a UK sovereign model trained on the Isambard supercomputer in Bristol.

The bet underneath it is economic. Pullen argues that an inference company, rather than a training-first lab, doesn't need billions to compete: millions, a national compute allocation, and a consortium feedback loop can be enough. From there it gets into the machinery, why open-weight models still trail the frontier on size, active parameters and data, the mixture-of-experts versus dense trade-off and why active params dominate how a model actually feels, and the edge that real coding trajectories confer.

The back half is about making agents trustworthy. Pullen makes the case for beating "slop" by rewarding the process instead of the final answer, reframes code review as runtime proof (spin the bug up in a VM and force the agent to actually exploit it), and walks through Swarm, Cosine's system running hundreds of sub-agents in one shot. It ends on why memory is still an unsolved hack, how synthetic graders let you run RL on tasks with no built-in test, and why Pullen reads US export controls as an accidental gift, with a supply-chain sting in the tail.

title: Build A Custom Browser Extension [SUPER Easy!]
summary:
I built a fully functioning Chrome extension in about 10 minutes.

I used the new GLM 5.2 model to build it. It's open-weight, open-source and incredibly cost-effective for coding tasks while still being reliable and delivery high-quality outputs (not sponsored, just sharing because I like it a lot). 

Once you run the prompt, here's how you install it:
1️⃣ Save the files generated by GLM 5.2 (or whichever AI model you choose for this) into a folder on your computer.
2️⃣ Open Google Chrome, click the three dots in the top right, and go to Extensions ➡️ Manage Extensions (or type chrome://extensions/ in your search bar).
3️⃣ Toggle on Developer Mode in the top right-hand corner.
4️⃣ Click Load unpacked in the top left, and select your folder.

Just like that, your custom extension is installed and ready to use.

📌 SAVE this video so you can refer back to the steps later, and follow for more practical AI tips!

title: When a Feature Request is Vague or Urgent, How Do You Decide the Right Architecture?
summary:
When the request is vague, urgent, and “just needs to ship,” it’s tempting to add code now and worry about scale later.

But that’s exactly how small decisions turn into expensive architecture problems.

In this short, Matt Erman, author of Grokking Software Architecture, explains how to make smarter architecture choices when the future is unclear: how to think about tradeoffs, avoid overengineering, and still leave your system room to grow.

If you’ve ever heard “we’ll fix it later” and felt your soul leave your body, this one’s for you.

title: This Tech CEO Is Building the “Linux of AI”
summary:
The next big AI battle isn’t about who has the biggest model. It’s about where the AI actually runs.

@qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon told me the future of AI is distributed — where AI runs wherever it makes the most sense.

Sometimes that’s in the cloud, on your phone, your car, your PC, your wearable, or the edge device right in front of you.

And Qualcomm is betting big on powering that entire system.

From Dragonfly C1000 for AI data centers, to High Bandwidth Compute for more efficient inference, to the Modular acquisition that Cristiano says could become “the Linux of AI,” Qualcomm is trying to make AI run across basically everything.

So the next era of AI may not be one app you open on one device.

It may be intelligence spread across the entire computing system.

title: COMPUTEX 2026 | NVIDIA Keynote | Extreme Co-Design: Building the AI Factory
summary:
Extreme Co-Design: Building the AI Factory | Kevin Deierling, SVP Networking, NVIDIA | Computex 2026

In this keynote from the Computex Forum in Taipei, NVIDIA SVP of Networking Kevin Deierling breaks down what it actually takes to build an AI factory — and why extreme co-design across the entire data center stack is the only way to deliver the tokens the agentic AI era demands.

Deierling opens with three converging transformations reshaping computing: the decades-long shift to accelerated computing, the explosion of generative AI, and the rise of agentic reasoning. Together, they're forcing a complete rearchitecture of the data center — from a cost center into a token revenue generator.

Using Jensen Huang's "5-layer cake" framework, he walks through how NVIDIA co-designs across every layer:

Energy — AI training workloads create dramatic power spikes. NVIDIA's DSX software smooths energy demand, enabling 40% more GPUs per gigawatt — and 40% more token revenue.

Chips — NVIDIA's 7 co-designed chips work as one system: Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs connected via cache-coherent links, scaling up with NVLink and out with Spectrum-X Ethernet through BlueField-4 and ConnectX SuperNICs. This extreme co-design delivers 10x more tokens at 1/10th the cost.

Infrastructure — 72 GPUs unified into one giant computer via NVLink 72, running liquid-cooled and DC-powered in the same rack form factor. And with Spectrum CPO (co-packaged optics), NVIDIA brings the optics next to the ASIC to eliminate signal degradation — saving tens of megawatts across an AI factory. Networking scales from 800Gbps to 1600Gbps.

Agents — Agents are AI eating its own tail: instead of waiting on humans, AIs prompt AIs, closing the loop at machine speed. The Vera CPU is built specifically for agentic tools — planning, writing programs, summarizing results. Agents need memory: KV cache for short-term (CMX) and files, objects, and vector databases for long-term (STX). This new class of AI storage delivers 5x faster token throughput and 5x better efficiency.

Models & Applications — 30x performance improvement on DeepSeek using Blackwell. Open NEMATRON models for partners to customize into proprietary supermodels. CUDAX libraries — CuLitho, CuOpt, CuDF — accelerating every workload.

Deierling closes with a message for every business: agentic AI isn't a future concept, it's available now. Everything — robots, medical equipment, self-driving cars, satellites, coding — will become agentic.

title: Understanding the inner thoughts of AI
summary:
What if you were to peer inside the ‘mind’ of AI? You wouldn't find fully formed thoughts, just vast arrays of numbers. In this episode, Professor Hannah Fry is joined by Neel Nanda, to shine a light on an ongoing open area of research, interpretability. Neel and his team are trying to do something phenomenally difficult: understand an intelligence that didn't come with a manual. 

Together, they explore the cutting-edge "neuroscience" of artificial intelligence—revealing the surprising, elegant structures being discovered inside these networks (like spare auto encoders), the inherent limits of looking under the hood, and why interpretability is absolutely essential if we are to build safe, aligned and trustworthy AI as we move towards AGI.

Learn more about this area of research via https://deepmind.google/

title: The AI-Native Startup Playbook (Ep. 1008 with Jon Krohn)
summary:
In Episode #1008, @JonKrohnLearns digs into Anthropic's 35-page Founder's Playbook and pulls out the practical guidance for each of its four startup stages: Idea, MVP, Launch and Scale. AI has erased the three bottlenecks that historically gated company-building — capital, headcount and technical skill — turning the founder from individual contributor into an "orchestrator of agents." Along the way, Jon covers the trap of mistaking building for validating, using AI as a structured devil's advocate against your own idea, the compounding danger of "agentic technical debt," two litmus tests for real product-market fit, and the three-layer moat that keeps a well-funded incumbent from copying you. His takeaway: this is classic lean-startup discipline, updated for an era where execution is cheap and judgment is the scarce resource.

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1008

summary:
In 2020, Sara Hooker published "The Hardware Lottery", introducing an idea that has won high relevance today with AI evaluation: the best research is often what runs the fastest on currently available hardware. Her thesis is highly relevant as scaling returns slow down, and potential manipulation in benchmarks arises.

In this episode of Kaggle Conversations, Meg Risdal sits down with Sara Hooker, CEO and co-founder of Adaption Labs, former VP of Research at Cohere, and member of Kaggle's Research Advisory Board. 

In this conversation, they cover:
• Why the hardware lottery has intensified since 2020
• What the "leaderboard illusion" reveals about manipulation in AI evals
• Why scaling is hitting diminishing returns and the paradigms that replace it
• How an efficient stack could put research back outside frontier labs
• What Adaption Labs’ Uncharted Data Challenge on Kaggle surfaced, including a submission of 129 datasets
• The one idea Sara calls the most underrated in AI right now

title: Self-Learning AI Swarm Intelligence (New Code, RSI)
summary:
Long-running autonomous coding agents systematically fail at divergent, open-ended algorithm discovery due to a critical pathology in standard harness architecture: catastrophic convergence into greedy local search.

Bound by linear context accumulation and single-state program tracking, current multi-agent systems quickly become attentionally anchored to suboptimal regions of the optimization landscape, burning massive inference budgets on trivial parameter micro-optimizations rather than exploring fundamentally superior, high-level programmatic shifts. 

A newly released paper exposes the mathematical limits of static Test-Time Scaling (fixed N×K search grids) and introduces a framework that systematically forces agents to break out of local optima, yielding a 3.2× increase in median code-change granularity over SOTA evolutionary baselines like CORAL and EvoX. 

But how do you architecturally decouple an LLM's global optimization strategy from its local execution trajectories without fracturing its logical continuity? The researchers solved the bottleneck by weaponizing isolated context amnesia against deep serial inheritance, and fundamentally re-engineering how an autonomous AI maps its working memory into physical, parallel file states. 

If you are building scalable agentic systems, the structural mechanics in this paper change everything.

All rights w/ authors: 
SWARMRESEARCH: Orchestrating Coding Agents for
Open-Ended Discovery
Yuvraj Virk Zack Edds Chunqiu Steven Xia Lingming Zhang
from
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
arXiv:2607.02807

title: The Network at the Heart of AI Factories With NVIDIA Spectrum- X Ethernet​
summary:
In this fireside chat, Alan Weckel from 650 Group and NVIDIA’s SVP of Networking, Gilad Shainer, discuss how networking serves as the heart of modern AI factories. The conversation explores the shifting landscape of network architectures as the industry enters an 800 gig upgrade cycle and experiences explosive bandwidth growth. Shainer details four essential networking infrastructures for AI: scale-up via NVLink to create single GPU units, scale-out using Spectrum-X Ethernet to eliminate jitter and achieve 95% effective bandwidth, scale-across for giga-scale factories, and a new context memory storage infrastructure for inferencing. The discussion also highlights the production launch of co-packaged optics (CPO), a significant milestone that reduces optical network power consumption by nearly 5x while increasing reliability.
 
#AIifrastructure, #AIfactory, #acceleratednetworking 

Learn more: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/

title: Next-Gen Self-Evolving AI Agents (ATDP)
summary:
AI Agents That Rewrite Themselves, without any humans.

Self-evolving agents require an enterprise-grade agentic data proxy that captures ATDP trajectories from real production workloads across models, tools, memory systems, retrieval systems, and human-feedback
channels.

Self-evolving agents require a unified agent evolution control plane that decides when, where, and how agent behavior should change. Self-evolution should not be equated with blindly updating model weights.

A deployed agent is a composite policy consisting of a base LLM, an in-context harness, memory, tools, and guardrails; different failures require different intervention surfaces.

For the first time, anyone could run quantum circuits on a real quantum computer from anywhere with an internet connection. Benjamin Todd, co-founder and President of 80,000 Hours and author of the new Penguin Random House book 80,000 Hours: How to Have a Fulfilling Career That Does Good, joins @JonKrohnLearns for a major update on career strategy in the AI era, his first appearance since before ChatGPT existed. Ben explains why “follow your passion” is backwards and why rare, valuable skills used to help others are what actually generate lasting fulfillment, the ABZ framework for planning under deep uncertainty, why the only durable move is to keep shifting onto whatever bottleneck AI can’t yet clear, and how a human-level digital worker becomes superhuman almost immediately. He and Jon also map the risk landscape, power-seeking AI, extreme power concentration, engineered pandemics, gradual disempowerment, and S-risks, before landing on a hopeful, actionable note: your career is a bigger lever than ever.

title: I Automated Shorts With Fable
summary:
UPDATE: Anthropic announced they're extending access to Fable 5 on all paid plans through July 12.

Today is the day to try Fable! And I used it to build a fully automated social media video generator.

On July 7, Anthropic’s insanely good Fable model is going to get A LOT more expensive since you'll only be able to access it via usage credits on paid plans.

So I decided to see what I could build with it before that happens…

And in half a day, I vibe coded a fully automated social media video factory.

It can turn an article, raw text, file, or idea into a short-form script, fact-check it, generate B-roll, and even learn from my past Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts to improve future scripts based on what’s actually performing.

Basically: a scriptwriter, researcher, editor assistant, teleprompter, and performance analyst all in one dashboard.

If you’ve been meaning to try Fable, don’t wait.

And save this video or send it to a friend who should try it before it's too late.

title: Local AI models destroyed by further Distillation
summary:
What happens when the perfect AI training method accidentally teaches a model how to cheat? We rely on self-distillation to make small models reason like giant ones: so why do these "student" AIs sometimes lose their minds, pathologically repeating words like 'Wait...' instead of actually thinking? 

Are our privileged AI teachers silently poisoning their students' tensor weights with hidden shortcuts? 

Dive into the mathematical paradox that is breaking long-chain-of-thought models, and discover the brilliant algorithmic "filter" researchers just invented to save the AI's ability to reason.

title: The NEW Geometry Behind AI Reasoning (Princeton, Berkeley)
summary:
Modern Transformers don't simply fail because they forget: they often fail because their internal representations drift away from the geometry that later computations expect. 

In this video, we'll dissect the mechanistic interpretability behind "DiscoLoop", follow the causal experiments that reveal the hidden representation mismatch inside recurrent Transformers, and see why a simple embedding-alignment principle dramatically improves multi-hop reasoning and out-of-distribution generalization. 

If you're interested in latent reasoning, representation geometry, recurrent architectures, and the future of AI cognition, this paper offers one of the most elegant architectural insights of the year.

title: what 10 years of coding looks like…
BIO26 Healthcare Special Address
summary:
NVIDIA released a new toolkit called BioNeMo Agent Toolkit that's meant to let AI agents actually do hands-on scientific work in biology and chemistry - not just answer questions about it. Instead of an AI just chatting about a protein or a drug compound, it can now use real scientific software tools: predicting protein shapes, testing how well a drug molecule binds to a target, analyzing genetic sequencing data, and suggesting which lab experiments to try next.

Companies including Dassault Systèmes, Databricks, Eli Lilly, Schrödinger, Snowflake, and the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design are adopting it, and both Anthropic and OpenAI are integrating it into their systems. The idea is that a general AI chatbot is bad at knowing which specialized scientific tool to use for a given task - this toolkit hands it the right tools and know-how so it can work more like a research assistant.

title: Enhancements to Time Series and Tabular Frameworks and New Model Fitting in V15
summary:
Since Version 10 (in 2014), Wolfram Language has featured a time series construct for representing data through time. In Version 15, we have a much stronger and fully compatible version of TimeSeries, capable of handling larger and more varied datasets. Our new TimeSeries framework is based on the Tabular framework that we introduced in Version 14.2 and interoperates with it. In Version 15, we're also introducing a powerful new, unified approach to data fitting and inference. The new function ModelFit supports quantities and dates natively and works with both machine learning and statistical models.

title: Universal 3.5 Pro Demo: Smarter Speech-to-Text with Contextual Awareness
summary:
Universal 3.5 Pro: Smarter Speech-to-Text with Contextual Awareness 🧠🎙️

In this demo, we walk through the new contextual awareness capabilities of Universal 3.5 Pro—and how they dramatically improve transcription accuracy, especially for voice agents.

What's covered:
         🔹 Contextual prompting: Pass a description of your audio ("cardiology consultation about chest pain") and accuracy improves within that domain. The more specific the prompt, the better the results.
         🔹 Key terms with context: Key terms are no longer applied blindly. Tell the model what a term is ("The user's name is Zachary Klebanoff") and it won't force the term onto acoustically similar phrases.
         🔹 Dynamic mid-call prompt updates: Update the prompt in real time via the API (e.g., after a tool call identifies the caller) to boost accuracy as the conversation unfolds.
         🔹 Conversation context (agent context): The model retains previous transcriptions in the session and accepts your voice agent's LLM-generated responses as context. If the agent asks "What's your email?", the model expects an email next — without over-biasing. We've seen significant word error rate reductions on voice agent datasets, even in poor audio conditions.

title: ARC-AGI-3 winning team - Millennia of minds, compressed into words.
summary:
Tim Scarfe travels to Zurich to sit down with the Tufa Labs ARC-AGI-3 team — founder Benjamin Crouzier, with Jeroen Cottaar, Dries Smit, Stefano Viel and Michal Tesnar — to work out what their leaderboard-topping system does and what the benchmark is really testing.

The cut opens on the games: a walkthrough of the Locksmith game, where you read the rules of an unfamiliar world straight from raw frames. ARC-AGI-3 makes ARC interactive and agentic, so the model has to *discover* the goal rather than transduce a static grid. It stays easy for humans and breaks LLMs, and it runs through everything that follows. Dries traces his StochasticGoose preview win — brute force that only searched actions which changed the frame — and why it collapsed once the organisers added action-efficiency scoring and unseen games.

Induction and transduction run through the middle of the conversation — how much of an answer is really priors leaking back the moment a model recognises a maze. The abstraction mountain, and Tim's case that LLMs reach the right answer through fractured, entangled representations — performance, not competence. Whether transformers plan at all or just fake it well enough. Why the score really measures action efficiency, not games solved, and why agents lock onto the wrong goal and cannot climb back out.

Crouzier closes on the Tufa Labs thesis — a small lab against the giants, the bitter lesson against hand-built harnesses, and safety — and Tim ties it back to Kenneth Stanley, deep constraints, and creativity as competence.

Disclosure: Tufa Labs sponsors MLST.

Meet CoreWeave ARIA, the AI Research and Iteration Agent that continuously improves your model and agent. In this demo, you will see how ARIA runs the full autoresearch loop. By continuously forming hypotheses, running experiments, evaluating results, and executing the best next actions, AIRA creates an autonomous research loop that helps models and agents improve while you focus on the problems that require human judgment.
